instructions: In a small bowl, stir together the 1 tbsp paprika, 1 tsp brown sugar, 3/4 tsp salt, 3/4 tsp onion powder, 3/4 tsp garlic powder, 1/4 tsp cayenne, 1/2 tsp oregano and 1/2 tsp thyme.
Cut the 1.5 lb salmon into 4 pieces if it isn't already. Lay them skin side down on a plate and pat the tops very dry with paper towels.
Melt 2 tbsp of the butter and brush it over the flesh side of the salmon. Sprinkle the spice mix evenly over the buttered side and pat it on so it sticks.
Squeeze 2 tbsp of juice from half the lemon and cut the other half into wedges. Stir the lemon juice and the 1 tbsp honey together in the empty spice bowl. Chop 1 tbsp of the parsley.
Turn on the fan over the stove. Heat a large cast iron skillet over medium heat with nothing in it for about 3 minutes, until a drop of water dances on the surface.
Lay the salmon in the pan spice side down, one piece at a time. Leave it alone for 2 to 3 minutes, until the spices have turned dark and crusty. Expect some smoke.

Flip the pieces onto the skin side and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until the skin is crisp. If you have a thermometer, you're cooking it to 145°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Press the thickest piece with a fork: it's done when it flakes and there's no see through center left. Move the salmon to plates.
Take the pan off the heat. Stand back and pour the 1/4 cup broth in at the edge of the pan. It'll steam hard.
Add the lemon and honey mixture and the remaining 2 tbsp butter. Stir until the butter melts and the sauce is smooth, about 30 seconds.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the lemon. Spoon it over the salmon and scatter the parsley on top.
Serve over rice with the lemon wedges.
method_notes: All three coat dry salmon in a paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, thyme, oregano and cayenne rub and sear it spice side down in a hot cast iron skillet until the crust goes dark. Well Plated adds a little brown sugar, brushes the fish with butter instead of oil, uses a dry pan over medium heat and cooks to 145°F; Primavera Kitchen starts the fillets skin side down in oil and bastes with butter. Cooking Classy makes a quick sauce in the same pan with chicken broth, lime juice, honey and butter. This follows Well Plated with the cayenne halved for a milder crust, the salt in table salt, and Cooking Classy's pan sauce made with the lemon from Well Plated.
